Environmental Data App

The Environmental Data App (EDA) is a portal where users can visualize and compare International Space Station (ISS) cabin, hardware environmental telemetry data, and radiation data gathered from spaceflight missions. On the Mission Dashboard the users can visualize temperature, carbon dioxide (CO2), and relative humidity measurements and radiation doses recorded in the ISS cabin and ground control for the duration of the mission. In addition to Temperature and Relative Humidity data collected from both flight and ground hardware units. The Mission Comparison feature can be used to visualize data across multiple missions. Raw and summary data are available for download on the Data Tables tab through the Data Tables section.


Rodent Research 18 (SpX24)

The purpose of this Rodent Research investigation is to characterize the impact of spaceflight on mouse retinal vasculature and tissue remodeling and study the role of mitochondria in regulating oxidative stress-induced cellular damage and cell-cell interactions in the function of the blood-retina-barrier (BRB). Also, determine the extent to which an antioxidant metalloporphyrin protects againstbspaceflight environment-induced changes in retinal neurovascular coupling and retinal function. The Rodent Research-18 (RR-18) flight experiment launched on SpX24 on December 21, 2021 at 5:06 am Eastern Standard Time (EST) from Kennedy Space Center (KSC). Forty male mice were flown in two Rodent Transporters and were transferred to four Rodent Habitats upon arrival to the International Space Station (ISS). The mice will receive weekly antioxidant or saline treatments during their stay abroad the ISS. Twenty six mice will return to Earth live in late January, 2022. Some of them will be subjected to a 6-month readaptation experiment at the PI's lab in Loma Linda University (LLU). Fourteen mice will remain on the ISS for ~85 days and will be euthanized and processed on-orbit with sample return on SpaceX-25. Ground Control (GC) and Vivarium Control (VC) groups are maintained at Roskamp Institute (Sarasota, FL) and will follow the flight timeline with a 5-day and 8-day delay, respectively.

For this release, the ground dates have been matched to the flight dates.
